newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Nat Bank launches bond for retail customers.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Nat Bank launches bond for retail customers.

text.p: The National Bank of New Zealand on Tuesday issued a bond for retail customers and said it was the first of the top five New Zealand banks to do so.
The bank said its bond closely mirrors New Zealand government bonds, with a fixed coupon and semi-annual interest.
The bond registrar is The Reserve Bank of New Zealand.
The bond will be issued in three tranches, maturing on April 15 in the years 1999, 2000 and 2002.
The minimum investment is NZ$10,000, with increments of $1,000 thereafter.
"The National Bank bond provides an attractive option for people seeking a longer term investment, with a fixed income stream," said Bruce Dick, the bank's director of customer sales and services.
"The bond will allow them to diversify their investment portfolio, with the option of trading the bond on the secondary market should they want to access their capital."
The bonds will be sold over the phone through the National Bank's team of investment specialists, and well as through brokers and financial advisers.
